extension.summary: No gaps. No stale scores. Age ratings you can trust.
extension.description: MetaMender quietly improves your video library in the background. It fills in what your scraper left empty (plots, episode titles, credits, taglines, genres and more) from TMDB and TheTVDB, in each folder's own language, with an optional fallback language for empty fields. It keeps scores up to date while new movies and episodes collect votes, from TMDB and IMDb, then leaves them alone once they settle. And it gives movies and TV shows an age rating in your own country's system, for ten countries. Items with an NFO file keep their values, and the Details window in the context menu shows where each value came from, can put an original back and can keep a value as it is. A short setup asks for a free TMDB API key, your library's languages and what to fill; nothing changes before it is finished.
extension.news:
v1.2.1 (2026-11-22) - Browsing your movies or shows while a scan runs no longer keeps reloading the list: the scan waits until you have not pressed anything for a minute - New Stop scan in the MetaMender context menu while a scan runs; the next scan carries on where it stopped
v1.2.0 (2026-11-22) - Choose which libraries MetaMender works on; each one gets its own settings page - Ticking a library switches nothing on, and libraries added later stay out with a notice - New Keep the original title option per library - Settings from 1.1 are converted automatically on first start; nothing in your library changes. If they could not be read, nothing is switched on and a notice says so - Fixed: on OSMC and other Kodi builds with Python 3.9 the add-on did not start - With the IMDb ratings module 1.1.0, IMDb ratings no longer start a download in the middle of a scan
v1.1.0 (2026-11-13) - Setup now asks which rating Kodi shows: your scraper's, TMDB's or IMDb's - Setup now asks where TV show plots and titles come from first - Setup asks whether to replace other countries' age ratings
